niche_preference_profile: This user most consistently prefers interfaces with strong, explicit structure and hierarchy, clear grouping into cards or sections, and layouts that make actions and information easy to parse. They often favor light or neutral surfaces with restrained accent colors, but will also accept dark themes when they are clean, high-contrast, and organized rather than flashy. They prefer spacious spacing, reduced clutter, and modular containment over fragmented or overly decorative compositions. They like clear labels, helper text, visible affordances, and obvious action states. They also tend to prefer subdued, refined control styling over loud, saturated, or overly promotional treatments, while still valuing a clearly dominant primary action when one is needed.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong visual hierarchy with obvious titles, subtitles, labels, section headers, guided flow, and clearly prioritized actions over flatter or weaker hierarchy.
Prefers content organized into clear cards, grouped sections, divided lists, or contained modules rather than fragmented panels, floating elements, or weakly structured layouts.
Prefers generous spacing, breathing room, and simplified compositions with fewer competing elements over dense, crowded, or visually cluttered layouts.
Usually prefers light neutral backgrounds and restrained accent usage, or refined charcoal dark themes, over saturated, neon, highly decorative, or overly promotional color treatments.

Prefers interfaces where actions are explicit and easy to understand, with visible labels, clear completion controls, and one well-defined primary action rather than ambiguous, hidden, or competing controls.
Prefers softer, more understated buttons, toggles, chips, and controls—such as muted fills, soft outlines, and restrained emphasis—over harsh, high-contrast, or flashy control styling.
Prefers visible labels above inputs, helper text, icons, badges, selection feedback, drag handles, and other recognition cues that make the interface more self-explanatory.
